intro.title: Interfaces — Contracts for Objects
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user profile system to understand how TypeScript interfaces work. You will learn that interfaces act as contracts or blueprints, defining the shape that an object must follow. The main technology you'll use is the TypeScript `interface` keyword to specify required properties and their types. By the end, you'll create objects that adhere to these interfaces, ensuring your code is more predictable and easier to debug.
intro.usecase: Interfaces act as contracts that define the shape of data structures in real-world applications. In a user dashboard, an interface ensures all user profile objects have consistent properties like name, email, and role. When building a product catalog, interfaces guarantee each product item includes required fields such as id, title, and price. This pattern is essential for API responses, form validation, and maintaining data consistency across components in large-scale applications.
